First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}y-{2}^{y} & =3{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y-{2}^{y}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({2}^{y}) & =6x \\ (1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2){2}^{y})(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =6x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,{2}^{y}) & =6x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6x}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\,{2}^{y}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
